title: structured output: constrained decoding backends - tokenizer & regex/CFG edgecases
author: Evan Chen
description:
Motivation: Constrained decoding (CFG and regex backends) has surfaced several tokenizer edgecases in production and in the OpenAI-compat structured-output path. This PR consolidates fixes and hardening across the CFG backend, regex backend, and tokenizer canonicalization so that constraints apply deterministically even when token boundaries do not align with regex/grammar anchors.

What this PR does: - Add a tokenizer canonicalization step used by both backends that normalizes variant whitespace and maps problematic bytepair splits to canonical tokens used by constraint matching. This reduces false-negative constraint matches with subword splits. - Improve regex backend: support lookbehind/lookahead anchoring that spans tokenizer boundaries using a token-aware matcher, and add a fallback partial-match heuristic when strict matches fail to allow streaming outputs to be validated incrementally. - Fix CFG backend issue where empty/non-terminal expansions could lead to runaway acceptance (fixes ENG-1187). Add guardrails to reject grammars with ambiguous epsilon cycles at parse-time. - Add opt-in runtime flag (constrained_decoding.strict = true|false) to toggle strict matching for customers who rely on exact-token enforcement for high-assurance outputs. Default remains permissive to preserve existing behavior. - Add a suite of tokenizer-focused integration tests covering edgecases: lookaround anchored regex, multi-token punctuation, emoji/token boundaries, and bytepair splits that previously caused constraint bypass. - Update OpenAI-compat structured-output adapter to canonicalize constraints before translation into backend queries, preserving existing compatibility but avoiding silent failures.

Compatibility and performance: Changes are backwards-compatible by default. Enabling strict mode can cause previously-accepted outputs to be rejected; documented in release notes. The token-aware regex matcher adds ~2% latency on constrained-heavy workloads (measured in benchmarks included), but removes a class of correctness bugs.

Testing and validation: - New unit tests under tokenizer/ and tests/integration/ that reproduce previously-reported regressions. - Integration run against sample canary workloads (structured-output test harness). - CI: unit and integration runs passed after two reruns for flaky e2e.

Related: ENG-1123 (structured-output regression triage), ENG-1187 (CFG epsilon cycle), SUP-4321 (customer report: tokenizer-split constraint bypass).

review_discussion:
Priya: Important fix, but can you clarify the default behavior for permissive mode and add a config example in the docs?

Evan: Added docs and a runtime flag with examples in sdk/openai_compat/structured_output.md and a note in the release notes. The default is permissive (best-effort matching) to avoid breaking existing customers unless they opt into strict enforcement.

Jamal: Regex matcher looks good; suggest adding a microbenchmark for token-aware matching.

Evan: Added a small benchmark to perf-canary and included numbers in the PR summary (~2% p99 impact on constrained-heavy paths).

Hannah: Tests look comprehensive. One nit about error message clarity when strict mode rejects output.

Evan: Updated error message to include which constraint failed and a short hint to toggle strict mode or inspect canonicalization mappings.
release_notes: Fixes tokenizer/constraint mismatches for constrained decoding backends (regex & CFG). Adds tokenizer canonicalization and a token-aware regex matcher; introduces opt-in strict mode for deterministic constraint enforcement. Note: enabling strict mode may reject previously-accepted outputs.
